StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterCardPlayed.issue: The copy is rebuilt from the class rather than cloned. JugglingPower.cs:48 is `cardPlay.Card.CreateClone()`, which reproduces the card's full live state; powers.py constructs `type(card)()` and replays `card.upgrade_level` upgrades onto it. Upgrade level is therefore carried and everything else is not -- a this-combat cost override (ConfusedPower/Snecko Eye, powers.py), an affliction (Entangled, Ringing, Smog, Bound, Galvanized, Tainted -- all ported), or a this-turn free flag would all be dropped. DORMANT only in the narrow sense that no test exercises it; the route is a Snecko-Eye or Tangled combat plus a Juggling trigger, both ported. Named trigger: any Juggling copy of a card carrying per-combat state. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the player-side leg moved off the sim's Hook.BeforeTurnEnd slot (`on_player_turn_end`) onto `after_player_turn_end`, which combat.py dispatches AFTER `_process_turn_end_cards` and the hand flush -- the sim's port of Hook.AfterTurnEnd (CombatManager.cs:1307), the dispatcher for AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292). VERIFIED 2026-07-27 by reading combat.py and this power's class in powers.py. WAS: the effect ran inside Hook.BeforeTurnEnd, so its order relative to the turn-end card effects, the flush and Stampede's turn-end auto-plays was hook registration order. The registration-order witness is doubly gone: StampedePower also moved, to `after_auto_post_play_phase_entered` (powers.py), which combat.py fires strictly before this slot.

guards.rationale: powers.py tests CardType.ATTACK before incrementing. Identical.

powers.py uses `== 3` too, not `>= 3`, so Juggling fires on the third Attack only and not on the fourth and fifth. Matching an exact-equality test rather than 'improving' it is the right call and the sim made it.

C# counts Attack CardPlaysStarted this turn belonging to the owner; powers.py calls combat.history.attack_plays_this_turn(). The owner filter is a single-player tautology. This is the mechanism that makes a mid-turn Juggling application count the turn's earlier Attacks, and the sim has it.
powers.py CardPileCmd.add_to_hand, which is the sim's generated-card path and fires on_card_entered_combat. Pile-verb semantics (MaxCardsInHand, index) belong to creature_card_cmds, not to this unit.
